title: So what's happening with Russia's new, long-delayed crewed spacecraft?
gist: Eric Berger reviews Russia's next-generation crewed spacecraft (PPTS / Federatsiya / Orel, now called PTK NP again), which has spent nearly 20 years mostly as renderings. Roscosmos chief Dmitry Bakanov says parachute drop tests start this fall, with Max-Q abort-type tests in 2027 and a crewed debut on Angara A5M targeted for 2028-2029. Berger is openly skeptical of those dates.

themes.theme: Two decades of rebranding, little hardware

insights.claim: Russia's next-generation crewed spacecraft has carried at least four names since 2009 (PPTS, PTK NP, Federatsiya and Orel/Eagle), and after nearly 20 years Berger describes it as more of a Potemkin village than a real hardware program.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Russian crewed-spaceflight capability is falling further behind its US competitors.

insights.claim: About two decades ago, Russia and ESA discussed a joint crew vehicle for which Europe would have supplied the service module for a six-seat capsule. Europe dropped out, and Roscosmos continued alone.

insights.so_what: Historical context for how Russia ended up isolated in human spaceflight.

insights.claim: New Roscosmos chief Dmitry Bakanov appears to have dropped the 'Eagle' name favored by his predecessor Dmitry Rogozin, and the vehicle is again being called PTK NP.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: A signal of a leadership reset at Roscosmos.

insights.claim: Bakanov told Interfax that parachute drop tests of the PTK NP spacecraft will begin this fall in Russia's Far East, with launch-pad emergency rescue mode tests later this year.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: These would be the first concrete hardware milestones worth tracking.
insights.quote: And in the fall, there will be a parachute drop and testing in the Far East.

insights.claim: Tests 'in the zone of maximum dynamic pressures' planned for 2027 probably refer to a Max-Q launch abort test, which Berger calls a significant step toward spaceflight. It is unclear whether real flight hardware, boilerplates or mockups will be used.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Use the 2027 abort test as a check on whether the program is real.

insights.claim: Russian officials are targeting a first crewed launch of the new spacecraft in 2028 or 2029, likely on the Angara A5M, but Berger warns the date is unreliable because promises Putin made four years ago about Eagle and the lunar program were not kept.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.quote: This is probably not a date to write down in ink just yet.
